text:
Players who allow for lineup flexibility is a really underrated skill

When people talk about how good a player is the focus is often on their individual strengths and weaknesses.

But the ability to be able to build and have elite two way lineups in the playoffs is basically a necessity to win a championship. 

So it’s not necessarily just about being a two way player but the ability to be a player that allows for lineup flexibility on both offense and defense.

Part of the reason the 2022 Warriors had so much success in the playoffs was because of Steph Curry’s unique impact in not needing elite spacing to lead to great playoff offense. The Warriors regularly had lineups with multiple non shooters and even sometimes three when GP2 was playing.

With this years playoffs OG stands out as this kind of player. His insane versatility defensively combined with being a good shooter and a positive on offense, unlocked the Knicks as a two way team.

No slight to him but guys like Ausar may have better regular season impact numbers than OG but building an elite two way playoff team around him is a more difficult task. We saw that it was more or less fine in the regular season for the pistons, but in the playoffs Ausar ended up hampering the offense quite a bit during some stretches. 

Obviously I do think this is something people already do value but I think it’s something that maybe should be even more valued than where the general consensus is at.

The Hawks' only NBA championship came in 1958, when the franchise was based in St. Louis, before the dataset's 1976-77 cutoff.
